title: Affine coordinate rings have finite Tor dimension from stalkwise finite Tor dimension
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $Y$ Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and $f:X\to Y$ locally of finite type. Assume every source local ring has finite Tor dimension over its image local ring [def-pc-perfect-morphism]. Let $U\subseteq Y$ and $V\subseteq X$ be affine opens such that $V\subseteq f^{-1}(U)$. Put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$, with $A\to B$ induced by $f$. There is $d\in\mathbf N$ such that $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(B,M)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ and every $j>d$. The empty affine open and the zero ring are allowed.

proof.text: put A = Γ(Y,U), B = Γ(X,V). The map A to B induced by f is of finite type because U and V are affine. A is Noetherian, so a finite polynomial presentation P = A[t₁,...,tₙ] surjecting onto B makes B a pseudo-coherent P-module, concentrated in degree zero. For a prime q of P outside the support of B, B_q is zero. Otherwise q corresponds to a source point y in V and B_q identifies with the source local ring. The hypothesis gives finite Tor dimension over the localization of A at the image prime. The localized polynomial algebra is flat over that localization and its fibres have finite global dimension, bounded by n. Tag 068X therefore makes B_q perfect over P_q. Tag 068W, applied to the bounded-below pseudo-coherent complex B[0], makes B perfect over P. A bounded resolution by finite projective P-modules is a bounded flat A-resolution, since P is flat over A. Choose d so that this resolution is zero below degree -d. Tensoring with any A-module gives Tor vanishing above d; compute Tor' with a projective resolution and compare it to this flat resolution. The empty affine source has B = 0 and permits d = 0; no bound on dim A is used.

mathlib_searches.query: Finite Tor dimension on affine coordinate rings from finite stalk Tor dimensions for a finite type morphism over a Noetherian scheme
A finite type morphism over a Noetherian scheme with finite Tor dimension at every stalk has finite Tor dimension on affine coordinate rings

from.place: Relative finite Tor part of the proper perfect pushforward argument descending from lem-sc-finite-duality; step 1 of lem-pc-perfect-relative-tensor-locally-bounded (Tag 069C, stalkwise finite Tor dimension to a uniform neighbourhood bound). Step 1 of lem-pc-stalk-tor-dimension-locally-uniform: polynomial presentation and finite Tor bound for the affine coordinate algebra.

theorem affineSections_finiteTorDimension_of_stalkwise
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hperfect : HasStalkwiseFiniteTorDimension f)
    (U : Y.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (V : X.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, U), ∀ j : ℕ, d < j →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, U)) j).obj
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (f.appLE U V e).hom).obj
          (ModuleCat.of Γ(X, V) Γ(X, V)))).obj M)
